title: Who should be baptised?
intro: Jesus told his followers to make disciples, “baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.” Christians disagree about whether babies should be baptised, how (sprinkling, pouring or immersion), and what baptism does.

views.label: Babies and believers: baptism gives new birth
views.summary: Catholic, Orthodox and Lutheran churches baptise infants because baptism is God’s gift of grace, washing away sin and bringing new birth, not something earned by understanding. The promise is “to you and your children” (Acts 2:39).
views.source: Catechism of the Catholic Church 1250–1252; Augsburg Confession, Article IX

views.label: Babies and believers: a sign of the covenant
views.summary: Reformed, Anglican and Methodist churches baptise the children of believers as members of God’s covenant people, as circumcision was given to infants in the Old Testament. Whole households were baptised in Acts.
views.source: Westminster Confession, Chapter 28; Thirty-Nine Articles, Article XXVII

views.label: Believers only, usually by immersion
views.summary: Baptists, Anabaptists, Pentecostals and many others baptise only those who personally confess faith. In the New Testament, they argue, people believed and then were baptised. Immersion pictures burial and resurrection with Christ.
views.source: Baptist Faith and Message (2000), Article VII; Schleitheim Confession, Article 1

views.label: Believers only, for the forgiveness of sins
views.summary: Churches of Christ teach that believers are baptised by immersion for the forgiveness of sins (Acts 2:38), as part of an obedient faith.
views.source: Everett Ferguson, The Church of Christ (1996)

common: Almost all Christians baptise with water in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and many recognise each other’s baptisms. Quakers practise no outward baptism, seeking the inward baptism of the Spirit.
